The challenge was called the Basel problem and it held off the best mathematicians in Europe, the Bernoullis included, for ninety years. Euler solved it in 1735, at twenty-eight, obtaining $\pi^2/6$ by a route so audacious that it took even them years to justify it. That $\pi$ should turn up in a sum with not a circle in sight is one of the most bewildering things in mathematics, and it is still talked about: that same sum, generalised, is the Riemann zeta function, and on it depends the most famous open problem left.
